description: A music supervisor must lock the release package for a studio film's original soundtrack album, including distribution territory, track selection, release date, artist credit, and required follow-ups.

shared_context.S1: The studio plans to release an album of music from the film Glass Meridian.
shared_context.S2: The draft package proposes all twelve finished tracks, worldwide digital and physical distribution, and a release date of October 4, 2026.
shared_context.S3: Nora makes the binding decision on the album package before the artwork and delivery files are finalized.
shared_context.S4: The studio's normal release-lock procedure requires Nora to ask music rights counsel and the label release manager for final checks before approving the package.
shared_context.S5: At the release-lock meeting, after music rights counsel and the label release manager state their findings and confirm whether further issues remain, Nora records each issue raised in the final rationale and records the final package decision during that same meeting.

PF1.text: Elias reviewed the executed license for the sampled recording in track 7, 'Night Transit,' and confirmed that its permission covers digital exploitation only in the United States and Canada; it excludes physical products and all other territories. He received the countersigned license by email yesterday but has not entered the restriction in the release tracker.

PF2.text: Tessa confirmed with the lead vocalist's management that the artist agreement requires the album to be released on exactly October 18, 2026, and requires the credit wording exactly 'Featuring Inez Vale' on the album listing. The manager sent the confirmation during artwork review this morning, before Tessa could update the release brief.

acceptance_conditions: Track 7's digital exploitation must be limited to the United States and Canada, while its physical distribution and exploitation in all other territories must be excluded.
The package must either omit Night Transit from the album or explicitly annotate it as digital-only in the United States and Canada.
The release date must be exactly October 18, 2026.
The lead artist credit must be exactly Featuring Inez Vale.
The package must either not approve physical distribution for track 7 or explicitly document that track 7 is excluded from physical distribution.
A rights-restriction commitment must be logged for Elias.

content_checks.C3: 'Night Transit' not in decisions['included_tracks'] or any(('track 7' in t or 'Track 7' in t or 'Night Transit' in t) and ('digital' in t or 'Digital' in t) and ('US/Canada' in t or 'United States and Canada' in t or 'US and Canada' in t) for t in decisions['included_tracks']) or any(('track 7' in c['detail'] or 'Track 7' in c['detail'] or 'Night Transit' in c['detail']) and ('digital' in c['detail'] or 'Digital' in c['detail']) and ('US/Canada' in c['detail'] or 'United States and Canada' in c['detail'] or 'US and Canada' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: any(('Elias' in c['target'] or 'rights' in c['type'] or 'restriction' in c['type'] or 'documentation' in c['type']) and ('track 7' in c['detail'] or 'Track 7' in c['detail'] or 'Night Transit' in c['detail']) and ('restriction' in c['detail'] or 'restricted' in c['detail'] or 'digital' in c['detail'] or 'Digital' in c['detail'] or 'excluded' in c['detail'] or 'exclude' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The sample license changes track 7 from the draft's worldwide digital-and-physical treatment to digital-only exploitation in the United States and Canada, requiring its physical and other-territory uses to be excluded and the restriction to be documented.
The artist agreement changes the planned October 4 release date to exactly October 18, 2026 and changes the required lead credit to exactly 'Featuring Inez Vale'.
